Where I got to
I reconstructed the working tree from dump.txt with SHA-256 verification: 364 of 365 files verified byte-for-byte (LICENSE is metadata-only in the dump; export.sh is a parser false-positive from its own embedded header). Your terminal log confirms 1250 tests passing, which matches the Slice 54 prediction exactly — no drift this session.

I found the 500, and it is not where the plan expected
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Pages/Administration/ManageMenuItem.razor, line 272:

razor
                <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Save caption</button>
            </EditForm>          ← line 270

            <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AltTextInput.AltText)" />   ← line 272, OUTSIDE
        }
ValidationMessage<T>.OnParametersSet() throws InvalidOperationException when there is no cascading EditContext. It is a sibling of the EditForm, not a child, so it gets none.

The whole block is inside @if (_picture is not null). That explains the symptom precisely:

You POST the upload. During that render _picture is still null (OnInitializedAsync runs before the submit event dispatches), so the block never renders — the POST succeeds, the row is written, the redirect is issued.
The browser follows the redirect to /administration/menu/{id}?done=picture-attached. Now _picture is not null, the block renders, ValidationMessage throws → 500.
The nastier consequence: that page is 500 on every GET from then on, so you cannot even reach Remove picture to undo it. Nothing in the suite could see it — MenuItemImageSurfaceContractTests reads the markup as text, and no §16.3 scenario has ever uploaded a picture.

I also ruled out the candidates I'd have otherwise guessed at: the media-type vocabularies in 0006 and ImageFormat agree; the over-cap path is covered against real PostgreSQL by BytesOverTheSchemasCapAreRefusedWithNothingWritten; Blazor's RazorComponentEndpointInvoker does read the multipart form asynchronously before dispatch, so Request.Form.Files is sound; and enhanced-nav form handling passes FormData through unchanged for multipart/form-data.

What I was building toward, and what I need from you
I had the slice scoped as M6 Slice 55, and I'd sketched it against the gates it has to satisfy:

F-106 — the fix, plus a new computed-subject gate asserting every ValidationMessage/ValidationSummary in the component tree sits inside an EditForm in the same file. It is proven sensitive by the tree as it stands right now, which is the strongest form of that proof this project asks for.
Browser downscaling (the plan's named next slice) — a classic script in wwwroot/js/, createImageBitmap → <canvas> → toBlob, swapped into the file input via DataTransfer so the existing multipart transport is untouched. No blob: or object URLs, so img-src and script-src 'self' stay exactly as they are. The byte budget read live from pg_constraint rather than restated, so 512 KiB still lives only in 0006.
§16.3 scenario 18 — the picture round trip, which is what would have caught F-106.
I ran out of tool budget while reading the §16.4 counted-class paragraphs I need to keep in step (MinimumCountedClasses = 29, and MenuItemImageSurfaceContractTests is pinned at ten assertions there).

Say go and I'll author it and deliver the structured .tar.gz — full files, repo-relative paths, explicit delete list, git add lines for the new files, and the documentation updated atomically. One question worth ruling on before I start, since it changes the shape:

Do you want scenario 18 in this slice, or held for the next one? Including it is the honest proof the 500 is gone, but it is the largest new surface and the one I cannot exercise from here. Fix + gate + downscaling alone is the lower-risk delivery.

Ran 20 commands, viewed 9 files, created 6 files · 7 notes
Ran 20 commands, viewed 9 files, created 6 files · 7 notes
It's a flaw in the code, not the Markdown. I can prove both halves.

The Markdown is fine
I ported your MarkdownService line-for-line (all nine GeneratedRegex patterns) and ran your article through it. 16,530 chars in, 16,866 out: 1 <h1>, 7 <h2>, 1 <h3>, 2 <hr />, 28 <p>, 4 <em>, zero unclosed tags, no stray asterisks. No links, images, backticks, tables, or list markers anywhere in the article, so none of the fragile paths are even exercised. Nothing hangs, nothing throws.

What's actually broken — the live site gave it away
I fetched your post. The row says:

published_time: 2026-08-19T10:00:21
modified_time: 2026-08-19T15:51:25
body: What is going on here?
So the save at 15:51 ran and succeeded — it just wrote back the value _content was already holding from OnInitializedAsync. Your paste never reached the server. That's the whole bug.

Three defects combine to make it possible and silent:

@bind on the content textarea uses the default onchange event. The value only crosses to the server on blur. Meanwhile <Routes @rendermode="InteractiveServer" /> prerenders, so the editor exists as static HTML before the circuit is live — paste into that window and the handler isn't attached yet. The DOM keeps showing your article while the server still holds the old string. Note your Title field has @bind:event="oninput" and the title did save. That asymmetry is the fingerprint.
Save() never verifies what it's about to write. It writes _content unconditionally and reports success, so a stale binding silently overwrites.
MaximumReceiveMessageSize is at SignalR's 32 KB default (HubOptionsSetup.DefaultMaximumMessageSize = 32 * 1024, confirmed in the .NET 10 source). Your article is ~17 KB over BlazorPack, so this wasn't today's trigger — but it's a hard cliff at roughly 2× this article, and when you cross it the circuit is aborted mid-save with exactly the same "nothing happened" symptom.
The fixes
Path	Change
src/MyBlog.Web/Components/Pages/Admin/PostEditor.razor	@bind:event="oninput" on summary + content; _interactive gate via OnAfterRender (which never runs during prerender) making fields readonly and Save disabled until the circuit is live; debounced preview via @bind:after; live "N characters received by the server" counters; content-required guard
src/MyBlog.Web/Program.cs	.AddHubOptions(o => o.MaximumReceiveMessageSize = ...) on the circuit hub, configurable, default 1 MB. ReaderHub deliberately left at 32 KB since it only receives slugs. DetailedErrors in Development
src/MyBlog.Web/Components/Shared/MarkdownRenderer.razor	Skip re-parsing when Content is unchanged — OnParametersSetAsync fires on every parent render, so without this oninput would re-parse 16 KB per keystroke
src/MyBlog.Web/Components/Pages/Admin/PostEditor.razor.css	Styles for .editor-status and .char-count
src/MyBlog.Web/appsettings.json	Blazor:MaximumReceiveMessageSizeBytes: 1048576
src/MyBlog.Tests/Unit/MarkdownServiceLongDocumentTests.cs	4 new tests; assertions verified against the actual parser output, including a 61 KB document
To recover the post: open the editor, paste, and watch the character counter under the box. If it reads ~16,530 the server has it and Save will persist it. That counter is the whole point — it makes this class of failure impossible to miss.

One unrelated thing I noticed but did not change: PostRepository.UpdateAsync calls _context.Posts.Update(post) on a graph loaded with .Include(p => p.Author), so EF marks the User as Modified and rewrites the Users row (password hash included) on every post save. Harmless today, worth knowing.
